newsitem.title: UK: Harland & Wolff says H1 results encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Harland & Wolff says H1 results encouraging.

text.p: Belfast shipbuilder Harland & Wolff broke even in the first six months of this year and said its first half results were encouraging.
"It demonstrates that the strategy we have undertaken of focusing on opportunities in the offshore oil and gas industry is correct," a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
The group reported an operating profit of 0.8 million sterling in the first half of 1996 compared with a loss of 3.7 million in the first half of 1995.

Harland & Wolff made allowance for a loss on the sale of a subsidiary, Trassey Shipping, leaving it in a break-even position on a pre-tax basis. The company reported a pre-tax loss of 2.1 million in the first six months of 1995.
The half-year results were issued to shareholders in an internal document.
Harland & Wolff said it planned to continue to pursue business opportunities for new buildings and major conversions for both the UK continental shelf and further afield.

Earlier this year, Harland and Wolff won a 100 million pound order to build a Floating Production, Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel for BP Exploration and co-venturers, including Amerada Hess, in developing the Schiehallion oil field, west of Shetland.
It won another major FPSO contract later in the year when it undertook to convert an oil tanker into an FPSO vessel for offshore contractor Bluewater.
The company also won the multi million pound contract to repair the oil tanker Sea Empress which ran aground off Milford Haven earlier this year causing massive pollution.

Norway's Fred Olsen has a 47.5 percent voting stake in the Northern Irish shipbuilder. Management and employees hold a further 47.5 percent voting stake while the balance is held by a group of local investors.
